definitions.explanation: To reduce food such as vegetables or spices to fine pieces using a grater or similar tool, typically moving in a back-and-forth or circular motion.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}をすり{下|お}ろす。
{生姜|しょうが}をすり{下|お}ろして{薬味|やくみ}にする。
examples.english: I grate ginger to use as a condiment.

examples.japanese: リンゴをすり{下|お}ろして{離乳食|りにゅうしょく}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I grated an apple to make baby food.

notes:
USAGE: すり{下|お}ろす is a godan verb commonly used in cooking contexts. It is a compound verb combining すり (from {擦|す}る, to rub) and {下|お}ろす (to move downward), describing the downward rubbing motion of grating.

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive (takes を)

ASPECT: すり{下|お}ろしている indicates the action of grating in progress.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{大根|だいこん}をすり{下|お}ろす (to grate daikon radish)
・{生姜|しょうが}をすり{下|お}ろす (to grate ginger)
・{山葵|わさび}をすり{下|お}ろす (to grate wasabi)
・{人参|にんじん}をすり{下|お}ろす (to grate carrot)
・{林檎|りんご}をすり{下|お}ろす (to grate apple)

KANJI NOTE: Often written in hiragana as すりおろす. Can also be written as {擦|す}り{下|お}ろす.

RELATED NOUN: すり{下|お}ろし refers to the grated food itself, especially {大根|だいこん}おろし (grated daikon).
